items.basis: The candidate proposes a 120-micron second-stage wedge-wire screen to arrest scale particles causing clogging, but the problem record explicitly identifies "biological growth" as a co-equal clogging mechanism; biological slime and biofilm are soft, deformable, and pass through rigid mechanical screens or blind them without being removed by particle-size exclusion, leaving the mechanism fundamentally incomplete against half the stated failure cause. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "progressive nozzle clogging from scale particles and biological growth in the recirculated water"

The candidate claims automatic backflush keeps the cascade in service with "no mill stop," but during the backflush cycle on a single 150 mm supply header feeding 120 nozzles, flow is either diverted or pressure drops below the required operating band; if the backflush requires even a momentary flow interruption or dP sag below 13 bar, the boundary condition "13-15 bar; full design flow; no mill stop" is physically violated during every trigger event. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "Boundary conditions: 13-15 bar; full design flow; no mill stop"
No evidence bundle is held, therefore no internal contradiction between evidence and claims can be demonstrated from the record. GROUNDED_IN: EVIDENCE (none held)

The baseline does nothing; adding a two-stage wedge-wire cascade with dP-triggered backflush is a physical addition that alters the fluid conditioning upstream of the nozzles, making it demonstrably non-equivalent to the status quo. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "doing nothing new — the status quo the candidate must beat"

The candidate specifies installation via "flanged spool swap at a planned roll change" on the "150 mm supply," but a two-stage wedge-wire cascade with automatic backflush valving, dP transmitters, and control logic requires significant physical envelope and piping bypasses that cannot deterministically fit within a standard flanged spool piece without violating spatial constraints of existing mill header plumbing. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "flanged spool swap at a planned roll change"

The testable prediction relies on "the mill's clog log and roll thermography" to measure clogging events, but a clog log is an operator-maintained administrative record subject to inconsistent threshold definitions for what constitutes an "event," introducing unquantified subjective variance into the claimed 95 percent band of 1.0-2.0 versus baseline 4.1 plus or minus 0.6. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "by the mill's clog log and roll thermography"

intervention_suggestions.suggestion: Add a biocide dosing station or UV treatment upstream of the wedge-wire cascade to neutralize the "biological growth" mechanism, because mechanical screening alone cannot remove deformable biological matter identified in the problem statement. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "progressive nozzle clogging from scale particles and biological growth in the recirculated water"
